headline: Stanford and Infineon authors publish an open-source framework for mixed-signal FPGA emulation
fact: Steven Herbst, Gabriel Rutsch, Wolfgang Ecker, and Mark Horowitz published a framework combining msdsl model generation, svreal synthesizable fixed- and floating-point representations, and anasymod FPGA build and control automation. The paper demonstrates a DragonPHY receiver, a firmware-controlled flyback converter, and an NFC-powered chip. Stanford dates publication to August 4, 2021; the TCAD journal issue is dated July 2022.

sources.title: An Open-Source Framework for FPGA Emulation of Analog/Mixed-Signal Integrated Circuit Designs — IEEE CEDA
sources.summary: The publisher's society page describes msdsl, svreal, anasymod, the three applications, and the July 2022 TCAD issue. svreal supplies synthesizable numerical representations, not direct synthesis of ordinary SystemVerilog real variables.
